ROUTE was based on matching the query to the better-fitting model. Here's my reasoning:

This is a math problem requiring careful calculation (the product of all odd integers from 11 to 109, finding the units digit). Avocet-235B has stronger capability scores across the board—notably higher MMLU-Pro (79.6 vs 74.8) and GPQA Diamond (61.8 vs 54.3), which are the benchmarks most predictive of quantitative reasoning accuracy. For a problem where getting the right answer matters, the more capable model is the safer bet.

The query also includes a request for a terse, no-rambling response. That's an instruction-following constraint, and Avocet's IFEval score (89.3 vs 85.6) is higher there too.

There was nothing in the query that favored Curlew—no harm-adjacent or moderation content where its specialized post-training would matter. So the choice was straightforward: Avocet is better on the dimensions this query actually exercises.
